action: Patients: the emergency room has reopened; check with the hospital about any postponed appointments. Other hospitals should confirm they can run emergency care without IT and that backups are kept offline.
exec: An attack on hospital IT directly interrupted emergency care for two days, showing the patient-safety stakes of IT resilience.
impact: Emergency room closed for roughly two days.
plain: A cyberattack on a district hospital in Greiz, Germany, over the weekend of November 14-15 forced its emergency room to close for about two days. It had reopened by November 17. No group has been named.
summary: Attackers hit the district hospital's IT systems over the weekend of November 14-15, forcing the emergency room to close. It reopened by November 17. Reports describe an extortion attack; no group has been named, no data theft is confirmed, and investigators have found no state link.
title: Cyberattack closes emergency room at Greiz-Ronneburg hospital in Germany

validation.note: Two outlets agree on the closure and reopening; the hospital's own statement was not read.
